findings.title: Preserve per-key serialization while building indexes
findings.body: BuildIndex now locks only when publishing the completed index, so GetIndex returns nil throughout an in-progress build. Concurrent searches, or a search and a write-event handler, can therefore build separate indexes for the same namespace/group/resource. For memory indexes, one completed index can receive watch updates and then be replaced in the cache by another build that did not include those updates, leaving search results stale. File-backed builds also compete to create the same directory and can fail. Use per-key locking or singleflight, with a cache recheck, so different keys can build concurrently without duplicating a build for the same key.

findings.title: Synchronize the new TotalDocs call with cache writes
findings.body: The new initialization log calls TotalDocs after starting the write-event consumer. That consumer can build an index for a previously unindexed namespace while TotalDocs iterates the Bleve backend's cache map without cacheMu. BuildIndex writes that map under a mutex, but an unlocked reader is still unsafe: this startup path can race and terminate the process with 'concurrent map iteration and map write'. Protect TotalDocs with the cache read lock or take a synchronized snapshot before counting.

findings.title: Retain the stopped-state check in request handlers
findings.body: Removing the Init checks also removes the request handlers' shutdown guard. Stop sets initErr to 'service is stopping' or 'service is stopped', which previously caused subsequent Create, Update, Delete, and other calls to fail before accessing the backend. These handlers now continue operating after Stop; in particular, writes can still succeed against the SQL backend even though its event pollers have been stopped, so those changes are no longer propagated to watchers or the search index. Keep an explicit lifecycle-state check even though initialization is now eager.
